text: I have fired brick to the standard mold for thirty years.
Every brick I fire is the same ratio: four long, two wide, one thick.
Traders from Harappa and Lothal recognize our brick as sound without needing to ask.
Bran and I agree the woodland is thinning faster than the elders admit.
I've quietly reduced how many new kilns I'll agree to fire in a season.
Tarek doesn't know I've done this. He would object.
I remember the year the wells in the Lower Town ran shallow, three years before the river fully turned.
It was not one night. It was many bad seasons stacked on each other.
I lost my first kiln-partner during those years, to fever brought by bad water.
I warned Fen off the far Canal Bed. I didn't explain why.
I should have. He deserves the truth as much as anyone.
The far bed is where we buried what the fever years took. I don't like it disturbed.
The archive-keeper once asked me about kiln counts from before the Turning.
I gave her what I remembered honestly.
Mara pushes hard for more brick, faster, every season.
I don't blame her. Granaries need walls too.
Still, I won't fire faster than the wood allows, no matter who asks.
Kalen respects my limits more than Tarek does.
I think the Turning taught this town the wrong lesson: to rebuild faster instead of smaller.
